questions.q: What does MOC stand for in site planning?
questions.n: MOC refers to the Maximum Allowable Construction, related to the area on which a building can be built (MACA).

questions.q: In the National Building Code, Group A refers to what type of occupancy?
questions.n: Group A specifically classifies residential dwellings, which is the first group in the code.

questions.q: In the National Building Code, Group E refers to what type of occupancy?
questions.n: Group E classifies commercial spaces including shops, offices, and markets.

questions.q: In the National Building Code, Group J refers to what type of occupancy?
questions.n: Group J is reserved for secondary structures that support the primary occupancy.

questions.q: What is PD 1152 known as?
questions.n: PD 1152 is the foundational document for environmental management in the Philippines.

questions.q: The Philippine Environment Code establishes standards for which environmental concern?
questions.n: The code explicitly addresses the management and standards for the country's air and water resources.

questions.q: What is the meaning of IAPOA?
o: International Association of Philippine Owners and Architects
Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
Institute of Architects for Professional Organization Affairs
questions.n: IAPOA is the unified national organization of architects recognized by the PRC.

questions.n: The PRC has the legal mandate to accredit professional organizations like the UAP as the IAPOA.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a building with artificial (mechanical) ventilation?

questions.q: Which passive cooling strategy uses the movement of air over water to cool a space?
questions.n: Evaporation absorbs heat from the air, which is a key strategy for cooling dry air or creating microclimates near water.

questions.q: What is the term for a sun-shading device that is horizontal?
questions.n: Brise-soleil (sun-breaker) typically refers to these structural or applied shading elements.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a 'Light Well' in deep-plan buildings?
o: To provide natural light and ventilation to inner rooms
To serve as a structural core for elevators
questions.n: Light wells allow core spaces without exterior walls to access daylight and air.

questions.q: What type of roof is most effective for heat reflection in the tropics?
o: Flat concrete roof with dark waterproofing
Green roof with heavy soil moisture
Metal deck with black bituminous membrane
Steeply pitched roof with reflective coating/light colors
questions.n: Steep pitches allow hot air to rise into the attic space, while light colors minimize solar absorption.

questions.q: What is the most effective way to reduce 'Heat Island Effect' in urban planning?
o: Paving all streets with dark asphalt
Increasing vegetation and using permeable paving
Increasing the number of street lamps
questions.n: Vegetation provides shade and evapotranspiration, while permeable paving reduces thermal storage.

questions.q: In sustainable design, what does 'Gray Water' refer to?
o: Wastewater from sinks, showers, and laundry (excluding toilets)
questions.n: Gray water is relatively clean wastewater that can be recycled for irrigation or flushing.

questions.q: What is 'Active Solar Power'?
o: Orienting a building to face the sun
Using mirrors to light up a dark room
Painting walls black to absorb heat
Use of mechanical/electrical devices like PV panels to harness solar energy
questions.n: Active systems require external energy to move fluids or convert light into electricity.

questions.q: What is the term for the deliberate use of shade from trees to cool a building?
questions.n: Strategic landscaping can block direct solar radiation from hitting building surfaces.

questions.q: Which orientation receives the most intense solar heat in the afternoon?
questions.n: The afternoon sun is at a lower angle and the ambient air is already warm, making the West face the hottest.

questions.q: Antoni Gaudí is associated with which architectural movement?
questions.n: Gaudí is the most famous exponent of the Catalan variety of Art Nouveau, known as Modernisme.

questions.q: I.M. Pei is often associated with which architectural style?
questions.n: Pei's work is characterized by refined modernist geometry and the use of concrete, glass, and steel.

questions.q: Richard Meier belongs to which famous group of architects?

questions.q: Oscar Niemeyer was a key figure in the development of which style in South America?
questions.n: Niemeyer adapted the International Style into a uniquely Brazilian, sculptural Modernism.

questions.n: Section 33 mandates that architectural plans and documents are the intellectual property of the architect, even after payment.
